newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain's first frigate to arrive in July.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain's first frigate to arrive in July.

text.p: A former U.S. navy frigate which was donated to Bahrain has started its journey from the port of Charleston in the United States to the Gulf Arab state and is due to arrive in July, U.S. officials said.
"The frigate Sabha began its journey on Monday. It will arrive here in mid-July," an official said.
U.S. officials said the former USS Jack Williams, Bahrain's first frigate and worth around $56 million, was "a gift" in appreciation for Manama's close friendship with Washington.
"Bahrain has paid around $35 million for new equipment for the frigate and training of its crew in the United States," another official told Reuters.

U.S. forces were currently preparing for a new set of military exercises with Bahrain, said U.S. Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defence for International Security Affairs Frederick Smith. Washington conducts four annual exercises with the Bahrain Defence Force, he said.
"As I am speaking to you...our pilots and sailors are preparing for a significant tactical air exercise here in Bahrain," Smith said, but did not give details of the timeframe.
The manoeuvres -- Initial Link 97 -- would also include forces from Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates, he said.
Bahrain, which has a defence pact with the United States, is the administrative headquarters for the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet. The United States keeps about 20 warships in the Gulf.
